summary: Re-ran content-approval custom-permission regression suite after main agent's middleware + routers/content.py fixes. 10/10 tests PASS (added one new test to explicitly validate content_approval.edit does NOT grant content_library.edit). Had to apply ONE small follow-up middleware fix: the sub-route mapping only matched `/api/content/pending-approval` but the actual route is `/api/content/admin/pending-approval` — added that prefix. After this, every scenario in the review request passes end-to-end: override roundtrip, /auth/me/permissions merge, PUT /approval 200 with override, PUT /approval 403 without override, pending-list 200/403 with/without override, admin always 200, and content_library.edit still 403 for yannick.

Patched by adding the `/admin/pending-approval` prefix. Trivial fix, no action needed.

critical_code_review_comments: Middleware sub-route conditions are string-prefix based and easy to drift from the actual router. Consider centralising route→feature mapping or defining it declaratively on the router (e.g., APIRoute dependencies) to avoid the kind of mismatch fixed in this iteration.
Custom-permission merge is now duplicated between middleware and services/permissions.py — keep them in lock-step or extract a single shared helper.

rca of the issue: Main agent's it.178→179 fix added custom_permissions merging in PermissionMiddleware and remapped content-approval sub-routes to the `content_approval` feature. The remap condition was `path.startswith('/api/content/pending-approval') or path.endswith('/approval')` — but the real pending-list route is `/api/content/admin/pending-approval`, so the request still fell through to the generic `/api/content → content_library` mapping and the middleware demanded `content_library.view`. Fixed by also matching `/api/content/admin/pending-approval`. The approval PUT (ends with `/approval`) was already correctly matched by the suffix check.
